overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an April 14, 2025 notice that omitted reappointment candidate names and by missing the 14-business-day deadline to respond to a complaint; two other allegations were not reviewed.

allegations.summary: The April 14, 2025 notice listed only 'Annual Vote to Reappoint Board/Committee Members' without naming the candidates for reappointment.
allegations.key_passage: The Board admits, and we find, that the notice for the meeting held on April 14, 2025, should have included the names of the individuals to be considered by the Board.

allegations.summary: The notice also allegedly omitted candidate names for interviews and appointment to the Green Energy Committee and Parks and Recreation Committee.
allegations.key_passage: The complainant did not request further review as to these allegations and therefore we do not review this portion of the complaint.

allegations.summary: The complaint alleged the minutes of the April 14, 2025 meeting were insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: However, the complainant did not request further review as to this allegation.

allegations.summary: The Board allegedly failed to respond within 14 business days to the first Open Meeting Law complaint, filed May 12, 2025.
allegations.key_passage: we find that it did not respond to the first complaint within the time frame required by the Open Meeting Law, that is within 14 business days.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
